description: 1 staging, 2 main, 3 upper. The same rules apply on every level; a level differs only in its column values.

The places the device belongs to, by id (ADR-039 lane L4c): station_id of stations.csv (st:barn) or cp_id of interlockings.csv (cp:107). hartlib.places gives readers the names and writes the ids back, so a renamed station or control point changes no cp cell. Exactly one for an interlocking device: on staging the station that names its desk area, on main and upper its control point (CP and the lowest switch number until the owner names it). A line block (roles track, helix, part, loop_half, spur) and its occupancy sensor list the places they join, separated by a semicolon: the stations of the switches at the block's two ends, or a switch's control point when it is in no station, plus any station whose tracks column names the block, in stations.csv's then interlockings.csv's order (build_device_map.line_cp writes them). A block's occupancy sensor has its block's. Empty when the device sits in none. Empty on every turnout row, its LCC alias's too (owner, 2026-11-25): a turnout's place is its switch's in the switch lists of stations.csv (staging's desk area) and interlockings.csv (main and upper), which hartlib.devices.place gives, and hartlib.devices stops on a turnout row with a cp.

The kind of JMRI bean: turnout, fb (turnout feedback sensor), block, occupancy (a block's detector), mast, head (signal head) or sensor (a panel status lamp). A field row holds it too, and it must be its id's row's.

What the device is: turnout, lcc_alias, fb, os (the block through a switch's points), xover_corner, track, spur, loop_half, helix, home (a mast at a switch), intermediate (a mast between two blocks), hidden (a routing mast the panel does not show), head, spare (a detector with no block), panel_status or part (a piece of track inside another block, part_of). Readers test it, never a name prefix.

The device's key from the plan, not its name (ADR-033; hartlib.device_ids): switch:<n>, dcc:<n> and fb:<n>:N or R for a turnout, its LCC alias and feedback; block:<ends> for a track, spur, loop half, helix or part block, from the switch labels and legs at the ends of its strands (block:1B-3A:1/2, block:107B-107C#1, several strands joined by +); os:<n> for an OS block, os:<n>:A-<end> for a staging single crossover's half by where its leg A runs (os:7:A-13C), os:<n>:<leg> for a double crossover's corner by the schematic leg it serves (os:225:D, not the Layout Editor corner); det:<block id> for a detector, spare:<system_name> for a spare one; mast:<switch label>:<leg>:<east|west> for a home mast (at a staging crossover half, the half as its OS block has it: mast:7:A-13C:B:east), mast:<facing block id>:<east|west> for an intermediate or hidden mast; <mast id>:<top|bottom|single> for a head; panel:<item>:<system_name> for a panel lamp of panel_items.json. The builders write it on every row with a level, unique on its level; empty on a Store's level-less row. Stays the same when the user name changes. Every field row with a level is keyed by it with its level (hartlib.devices.KEY, naming-layers step 4), so a rename changes no key; a field row whose id the generated file no longer has stops the build (the owner moves its cells to the new id or drops them). The name store (hartlib.track_names) reads a track's name from the field block row of its block: id.

The public name under ADR-005, which is also the JMRI user name. The generated file names every row; a field row's user_name is the owner's name and wins on every level (naming-layers steps 4 and 7: the builder puts every field row over the device's generated row, and a device with no field row keeps the generated values). A rename lists the Operations Pro copies of the old name and, for a mast, warns that it needs a new SML discovery and panel approval (hartlib.device_changes).

How the device is in JMRI now: field (the physical device is in JMRI, so jmri_name is system_name), virtual (an internal stand-in; system_name, when set, is the planned device), none (this row gives no JMRI name) or spare (a field detector with no block).
The physical or planned device (M2T408, M2S1300, IH3332), or the JMRI name of a staging mast or head. Empty when nothing is planned. A draft while assignment is virtual.

The name JMRI and the panels bind the device by. Equal to system_name when assignment is field, except a staging turnout the tables bind by its user name. For a virtual device it follows hartlib.level_devices; a main or upper block's (and part's) is IB:C3:<nnnn>, which build_device_map.py copies from block_numbering.csv (hartlib.block_numbering, naming-layers step 8; a helix block's is empty, its beans are staging's).
The LCOS node number (the RF24 address) of the field or planned device.
A turnout's DCC address (an LCC alias carries its own). A field turnout's JMRI comment takes it as its second group (hartlib.names.jmri_comment); nothing parses it back out of a comment.
The node, port and output text of a device (Node: 4 Turnout: 0 | OU: 1 Ports: 1,2), without the DCC group. Empty when the row has a jmri_comment.
The JMRI comment of a device whose comment is not wiring text (a block's description, a mast's control point and switch, a build note). Empty when the row has wiring.
The link from the row to the drawing: the switch or track name the trial drawing used.
Text for people from the old device map: what the row is for, or why a device has no detector.
Occupancy rows: the blocks the detector serves, separated by a semicolon.

Occupancy rows: wired, planned, not_wired or none, whether the detector is in the field, planned on a node input, planned with no input yet, or not planned. Required on every occupancy row; a spare detector (role spare, no block) is none (owner, 2026-11-25), which build_device_map.py writes.
Block rows: yes when the block is a Dispatcher System station (the stop its JMRI comment carries).

Block rows of staging: the system name (ILB...) of the block's JMRI layout block, which JMRI numbered when the block was drawn, or the builder numbers for a staging block with no field row (as a part's, naming-layers step 7). On the main and upper levels, ILB<1000 + n> with the block's IB:C3:<n>, which build_device_map.py copies from block_numbering.csv (naming-layers step 8; empty on a helix block's row); the Layout Editor build makes the layout block by it.

Block rows the CATS desks bind (45 staging blocks): the block's CATS discipline, CTC or YARD (owner's cell, moved from cats/data/occupancy_bindings.csv on 2026-11-25). Empty on every other row. hartlib.occupancy_bindings gives the desk builders and the audits these blocks with their occupancy sensor; digicon_lib.load_disciplines writes YARD to the desks as CTC, a discipline CATS does not know.

Block rows: the block this row is a piece of, when the row is a piece of track inside another block (owner, 2026-11-20: a short piece between two switches is part of the lower-numbered switch's OS block, or the block block_overrides.csv gives it). A row with part_of has role part and assignment virtual: a JMRI block and layout block of its own (jmri_name, layout_block) on its block's occupancy sensor, with no occupancy row or detector of its own, and the device maps leave it out (hartlib.devices.OUT_OF_MAPS). The block it names exists and has no part_of itself.
Mast rows: the switch whose leg the mast stands at. Empty for an intermediate, anchor or buffer-stop mast.
Mast rows: the block the mast faces.
Mast rows: the blocks the mast protects, separated by a semicolon.
Mast rows: the way the mast looks, east or west.

The state its bean takes when the tables load: inactive on a detector, closed or thrown on a turnout (not its LCC alias). Today only main and upper rows carry it (naming-layers step 9): every detector inactive (the sensors-clear LogixNG) and every turnout closed, thrown where the main route runs through leg C (build_device_map.startup_thrown: 227 and 229). The Layout Editor build reads it for the startup LogixNG. Empty where JMRI's default stands.

The JMRI comment of the bean the Layout Editor build makes for a main or upper row (turnout, block, detector, mast, head; not an LCC alias, a feedback row or a helix block): build_device_map.py writes it (device_map_rows.bean_cells, naming-layers step 9) and the build reads it, so tables.xml holds this text. Empty on staging rows, whose comment the build makes from jmri_comment or wiring (hartlib.tables_build.bean_comment). Step 11 unifies the two (owner, 2026-11-23).

The script that writes the row (build_device_map.py, every level's rows with their masts and heads since naming-layers step 12, or panel_items.json). A writer rewrites only rows that carry its name and stops on any other. Empty means the owner keeps the row by hand. The allowed names are one constant in hartlib.devices.
One plain sentence saying what the device is.

A device not on the layout yet (no level): the beans as the PanelPro Store wrote them, as compact JSON (hartlib.jmri_bean.bean_json), which the build copies into tables.xml. Empty for every row with a level.
